newsitem.title: USA: Coastal Caribbean gets show cause order.
newsitem.headline: Coastal Caribbean gets show cause order.

text.p: Coastal Petroleum Co said Friday Florida's First District Court of Appeal has ordered the state Department of Environmental Protection to show cause why it would not immediately issue an offshore drilling permit to Coastal.

After a Florida Supreme Court ruling in favor of Coastal last month, the agency indicated its readiness to issue the permit, subject to Coastal's publication of a notice that could reopen repetitive administrative hearings, the company said.

Coastal objected to the publication requirement and, on August 27, petitioned the Court of Appeal to issue an order that would require the agency to issue the permit to Coastal without further delays.
A Coastal spokesman said the agency must respond to the show cause order within 20 days, with Coastal's reply to follow within 10 days.

Coastal is seeking to commence drilling operations on its 800,000-acre offshore leasehold along Florida's Gulf Coast. It is a majority-held subsidiary of Coastal Caribbean Oils & Minerals Ltd. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
